Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. Attaching our short security questionnaire (novellbio-sq-20251112.pdf) — mostly focused on where data is stored for hosted endpoints, retention policies for request payloads & logs, and deletion guarantees. A few of the specific asks:

- Can you confirm the geographic location(s) where request payloads and generated responses are stored for the hosted API (by region selection)?
- What is the default retention period for request logs, inference payloads, and any cached artifacts (prefix cache / KV cache)?
- Can Novell Bio request an immediate deletion of all data tied to an account or single API key? What is the timeline and scope (primary storage, backups, snapshots)?
- Are hosted API requests ever used for model training or improvement by Redwood?
- Which subprocessors are involved in storage/backup/monitoring for hosted API data?

We have an upcoming internal review on Monday and would like to include your answers. If you can attach a short residency/retention matrix, that would be ideal.

Regards,

Novell Bio

Anne — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear list of asks. I've pulled together concise answers below and attached a small CSV "rwd-residency-matrix-20251114.csv" that maps data types to storage location and retention windows for hosted customers. Summary first, details after.

Summary (short answers):
- Residency: Hosted API stores request and response data in the region selected at account creation for primary storage. For redundancy some operational metadata may be replicated within the same cloud region family but we do not route primary stored customer payloads outside the chosen region for normal inference.
- Default retention: Request payloads & generated outputs: 30 days by default (used for debugging, rate-limiting, and abuse detection). Request logs/metrics: 90 days by default. KV/prefix caches are ephemeral (TTL default 1 hour for caches created by our runtime unless customer has opted into session history features).
- Deletion: Customers can open a data-erasure request via support with proof of ownership — primary data will be removed from active stores within 72 hours; backups and snapshots are purged on the next backup lifecycle (typically within 30–45 days). For enterprise customers with contractual terms we can offer accelerated purge windows and attestation.
- Training usage: We do not use hosted customer request/response content to train models or improvement unless explicit opt-in is provided (opt-in is off by default).
- Subprocessors: Primary cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure depending on region) for object/block storage; our logging provider (managed ELK stack), and a separate backup provider (cloud snapshot service). Full subprocessor list and SOC 2 link below.

Detailed answers (Q-by-Q):
1) Geographic storage: Primary storage location is set during account provisioning (e.g., us-west-2, europe-west1). See matrix: column "primary_region" for each data type. For high-availability we replicate control-plane metadata within the same geographic boundary; no cross-continent primary payload storage for hosted accounts.

2) Retention periods (defaults):
- Inference payloads & generated outputs: 30 days (default). Customers can change to 0 days via support request, but 0 days will disable troubleshooting/history features.
- Short-term runtime caches (KV / prefix / session cache): ephemeral, default TTL 1 hour.
- Audit logs / Request metrics (non-payload telemetry): 90 days.
- Billing and subscription records: retained for 7 years for accounting/legal.

3) Deletion procedure and timeline:
- Step 1: Customer opens a case (support portal or security@redwood.ai) and provides account ID + ownership proof.
- Step 2: Engineering-run deletion job removes primary objects within 72 hours and returns a job ID.
- Step 3: Backups/snapshots removed during next backup retention cycle (standard window 30–45 days).
- Step 4: We provide an attestation report (PDF) after purge completion upon request. For higher assurance (e.g., contractual requirement) we can negotiate a 7–14 day backup purge window in Enterprise agreements.

4) Training & model improvement: Hosted API data is not used for model training or improvement unless a customer explicitly opts into our "data improvement" program; opt-in is done per-account and logged.

5) Subprocessors & encryption:
- Data at rest: AES-256 encryption, keys held in cloud KMS by default.
- Customer-managed keys: available through our KMS integration (link below).
- Subprocessors include: cloud object storage, snapshot service, logging provider, monitoring/alerting vendor. SOC 2 report lists full vendor inventory.

6) Region-locking / export for e-discovery: We provide exports of logs and payloads on request (CSV or NDJSON). For legal holds we can provide a time-bounded export; additional fees may apply for large exports.

Attachments: rwd-residency-matrix-20251114.csv — maps: data_type, primary_region, default_ttl, backup_retention, deletion_timeline.

If you want, Jonas and I can hop on a 30-minute call Thursday to walk through the matrix and where we can tighten the backup purge window for you.

Best,
Irene Choi

Redwood Inference

Tom / Anne — thanks for the follow-ups. Answers below and I've included links to our compliance assets.

1) Fingerprints & analytics:
- We may compute truncated fingerprints (hashes) of requests for deduplication and rate-limiting, but these fingerprints are salted and stored in the same primary region. They are not routed outside the primary geographic boundary for analytics by default. Aggregated / anonymized usage metrics may be computed in a separate analytics pipeline (regionally partitioned) but no raw payloads leave the primary region. If Novell requires a contractual addendum prohibiting even salted fingerprints outside the region, we can add that as a term for Enterprise agreements.

2) Per-key deletion:
- We support per-API-key erasure requests. Process: open a support ticket with API key ID and requested scope (payloads, logs, caches). Engineering issues a keyed purge job and returns a confirmation ID. Target timelines: primary data purge within 72 hours; backup purge within standard backup retention cycle (30–45 days).
- Backups & keys: When customers enable customer-managed keys (CMK) via our KMS integration, backups and snapshots are encrypted under those keys where supported by the underlying cloud provider. If you supply your own KMS keys, we do not retain the plaintext key and cannot decrypt after key revocation — that provides additional guarantees for long-term inaccessibility.

Compliance artifacts:
- SOC 2 report: https://redwood.ai/docs/security/soc2-report (contact security@redwood.ai for temporary access link).
- Subprocessor list and DPA: available upon request; we can provide a redacted vendor list for procurement.

If you want written language for procurement, Jonas can prepare a short summary paragraph with deletion timelines and CMK support that you can drop into your contract appendix. Otherwise, happy to schedule a quick call to finalize.

Best,
Irene

Redwood Inference
